name: MN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district with incumbent Tom Emmer running for re-election
Emmer's massive financial edge: $9.8M raised, $4.5M on hand vs. Chapin's $439K
No public polling and no expert ratings; Polymarket prices Emmer at 92%
model.rationale: The R+10 lean, Emmer's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 92% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or ratings to the contrary, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Chapin within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Emmer, would warrant moving the race toward Tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 6th District is a Republican-leaning seat, and Tom Emmer is seeking re-election as the incumbent with the weight of House leadership behind him. He has raised nearly $9.8 million and holds $4.5 million in cash, dwarfing Democrat Doug Chapin's $439,000 raised and $70,000 on hand. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

There is no public polling of the general election and no expert ratings list the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Emmer roughly a 92% chance of winning. The forecast expects Emmer to win by a double-digit margin, consistent with the district's partisan lean, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
